description.narrative: 73% people lack access to safe water in Satkhira due to salinity, arsenic, and climate change. People spend more than BDT 600 taka/month for fresh water or spend 2/3 hours daily in fetching water from far sources. We offer to establish a jar based water transportation system where fresh water from ground is extracted, treated, Jarred and transported using local vans to the doorstep of people. Quality of the water is better than current sources and the cost is less, contributing to safely managed drinking water and providing us an opportunity to serve 10000HHs and run sustainable business

comment.narrative: 20-01-2025: We operate two distinct business units. The first is our B2B (business-to-business) component, where we supply water to local vendors. The second is our B2C (business-to-consumer) component, in which we sell water directly to customers through a jar-based local delivery system. Our water delivery business is experiencing slightly raipid growth with daily customer acquisitions, despite challenges from low water pricing and government regulations affecting our financial performance. Our net loss has decreased from BDT 65,490 in December 2023 to BDT 52,870 in July 2024, indicating progress towards profitability. Initially pricing water at 15-20 taka for individual customers, we've since lowered prices to attract more customers. The climate change impact, uneven rainfaill and ongoing monsoon season has impacted demand as people harvest rainwater, prompting us to adjust our pricing strategy. We're currently revising our water pricing following recent approval from the BSTI, which may provide more flexibility in our pricing decisions and enhance our market credibility.

comment.narrative: 20-01-2025: This business specializes in the distribution of 20-liter water jars, offering a dependable solution for regions facing continual drinking water shortages. We provide high-quality, potable water with seamless doorstep delivery, prioritizing convenience and accessibility for our customers. Our services cater to two primary markets: business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C). In the B2B sector, we supply a wide range of organizations, including offices, hotels, restaurants, and industrial facilities, ensuring they maintain a consistent supply of safe drinking water. For B2C, we deliver directly to households, providing individuals and families with a reliable and convenient source of fresh water. Our focus is on addressing the critical water needs of both commercial and residential customers through tailored and efficient solutions. The development of our distribution network has undergone several phases of refinement. Initially, we partnered with 16 carefully selected vendors after assessing their operational capacity. Following a thorough cost-benefit analysis and evaluation of their business management skills, we narrowed the vendor count to 11. However, challenges related to jar management led us to further reduce the number of vendors to 10 in the second phase. Many vendors struggled with effectively managing the jars, prompting us to moderate the water supply until their capacity improved. In the first phase, 40% of our customers were served through these small-scale vendors, a figure that decreased to 30% in the second phase as we streamlined our operations. In the current and final phase of the project, we have strategically maintained 10 vendor points while shifting focus toward direct-to-consumer deliveries. This approach has significantly enhanced operational efficiency, with vendor-based distribution now accounting for only 20% of our operations. Although the number of vendor points has remained stable, we have expanded our ...

comment.narrative: 20-01-2025: In this phase, we conducted two comprehensive training sessions on Business Development and Water Quality, alongside two learning-sharing events, three stakeholder engagement events, focus group discussions, and two financial management education sessions to support participants in growing and sustaining their businesses. A total of seven entrepreneurs, consisting of five men and two women, participated, reflecting our commitment to inclusivity. During the Business Development session, attendees learned strategies for business management, customer engagement, financial planning, and scaling operations. The Water Quality session focused on the importance of water safety, monitoring standards, and best practices for delivering clean, safe drinking water. The financial management education provided tools for budgeting and cost management to ensure economic sustainability. The learning-sharing events and stakeholder engagements facilitated knowledge exchange and collaboration among community members, local authorities, and key stakeholders, strengthening community involvement. These initiatives play a crucial role in empowering local entrepreneurs to grow their businesses while safeguarding public health and driving long-term development in the community.

20-01-2025: Our project has established a workforce of 52 paid positions, including a laboratory chemist, project staff, factory personnel, delivery teams, marketing officers, vendors, and their staff. This structure covers all operational needs from water quality control to distribution.However, we face a significant gender imbalance, with only 2 out of 52 positions held by women. This disparity stems from local norms discouraging women from operating vehicles in our area, as well as the physically demanding nature of jar distribution and service maintenance.Despite these challenges, UCL is committed to gender equality. We are actively implementing measures to increase female representation in our workforce, aiming to create a more inclusive environment that leverages diverse skills and perspectives across our operations.

actual.value: The business delivers 20-liter jar-based water directly to customers' doorsteps in regions facing persistent drinking water shortages. Its customer base is divided into business-to-business and business-to-consumer segments. Initially partnering with sixteen vendors, the operation was streamlined to eleven after assessing their capacity and management capabilities. Jar management challenges necessitated a further reduction to ten vendors in the second phase. The strategy now emphasizes direct customer deliveries in consumer-dense areas to enhance sustainability. Key adjustments in water pricing and broader operational strategies are on the way after getting the approval from Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution (BSTI). However, the impacts of climate change, uneven rainfall, and political events may temporarily disrupt water distribution. Efforts are underway to promote gender representation within the workforce. Despite financial challenges posed by low pricing and regulatory constraints, the project anticipates achieving profitability in the coming months. A jar tracking software has been implemented to streamline operations. Currently limited to the local market pending BSTI approval, expansion plans are in place to reach Satkhira and Khulna cities once approval is secured. The initiative consistently delivers 35,600 liters + 2000 liters (free of cost for local residents) of water daily, which is equivalent to 1,780 jars (without local recipients) while maintaining water quality within WHO standards. Notably, the direct delivery model significantly saves time for women, enabling them to engage in more productive activities. Overall, the project is poised for growth and efficiency, ready for expansion in collaboration with 1001fontaines.
